blocks.text: There are n iterations. Each performs one required-prior lookup and one current-prefix update, both expected O(1) under the stated hash-table assumption, so summing the per-element work gives expected O(n) time. In the worst case all n + 1 prefix values are distinct, so the frequency map stores O(n) entries and uses O(n) extra space.

Expected time is not O(1) or O(log n) because all n elements are scanned, and it is not O(n^2) because no earlier boundary is rescanned inside an iteration. Space is not O(1) or O(log n) because the map can retain one distinct key per boundary, and it is not O(n^2) because at most n + 1 boundaries—and therefore at most n + 1 distinct prefix keys—exist.
